audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].side read "Skill" while win[4] read "Taliyah", and the two whys argued with each other: the full layer said Emperor's Divide wins every 2v2, the content layer said her level 6 keeps her ahead through map pressure.
audit.why: Taliyah's R is Weaver's Wall (180/150/120s, 2500/4500/6500 range) — a travel and repositioning tool, not a lane kill. Azir's R at 6 is disengage, not a kill button either, so neither champion gains a kill threat; what decides the row is that she still clears the wave faster with Threaded Volley (7s down to 3s) and leaves first. The content layer is the coherent one.
audit.corrected: phases[4].side set to Taliyah and its why rewritten to match; the remaining rows already agree across layers.

audit.why: Spike structure is right: her pressure is early and roam-based, Azir's inflection is first item (Nashor's) and again at Rabadon's. Her R getting to 120s at rank 3 is what keeps her roam threat live all game.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single most important interaction in this matchup was nowhere on the page: Unraveled Earth (E, flat 14s) stuns anything that DASHES through it or is knocked through it — which means Shifting Sands is a trap, and Seismic Shove can throw you into her own minefield. breakdown.cooldowns also held no digit (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT).
audit.why: Riot's E text: "If enemies dash through it or are knocked through it, the mines explode and stun them." Azir's only escape is a dash, so his escape is also her stun setup. Real cooldowns: Q 7/6/5/4/3, W 14/12.5/11/9.5/8, E flat 14, R 180/150/120.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns field, dosFull[0].d and dontsFull[1].d now state the mine-dash interaction with the numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: The derived flags mark Threaded Volley and Seismic Shove as "grounding". Riot's own description of neither ability mentions grounding.
audit.why: The brief says to trust the description over a misfiring derived flag. I wrote nothing about grounding anywhere.

audit.whatIsWrong: Eleven fields called Taliyah "he/his"; dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim under unrelated titles; wants.foe[1] called Worked Ground a wall.
audit.why: champ-gender.js lists taliyah as female. Worked Ground is the terrain Threaded Volley leaves behind, not a wall — the only wall she makes is Weaver's Wall.
audit.corrected: Pronouns fixed, both bleed bullets rewritten to their titles, wants.foe[1] regrounded.
